title: File handling
examples: How do I make sure my program doesn't lose the information?
What is the difference between reading and writing to a file?
Why do I need to close the file after I am done?

explain.say: Today we will learn about file handling in programming.

draw.text: File Handling: open, read, write, close

explain.say: First we must open the file before we can do anything with it.

items: File Name: The path to the file

explain.say: Next we use the read function to get information from the file.
To save data we use the write function to put information in the file.
It is very important to close the file when you are finished working.
In real life when you save a document you follow these steps. You open the program, you write your text, and then you save and close the file.

draw.text: Saving a document: Open -> Write -> Close

faq.q: Why do I need to use the close function?
faq.a: Closing the file tells the computer that you are done with it. This prevents data corruption and frees up system resources.
asks: What happens if I forget to close the file?

faq.q: What is the difference between read and write?
faq.a: Reading pulls data from the file into your program to be used. Writing pushes data from your program into the file.
asks: Can I read and write at the same time?

faq.q: What happens if the file I want to open does not exist?
faq.a: Most programming languages will give you an error message. You must check if the file exists before trying to open it.
asks: What if the file path is wrong?
How do I handle missing files?

faq.q: Is the file open automatically when I start the program?
faq.a: No, you must explicitly use the open command. This is the first step in the file handling process.
asks: Do I need to call open first?
Can I skip the open step?

faq.q: Can I read and write to the same file in one program?
faq.a: Yes, you can, but you must be careful about the file mode. You might need to read some data then overwrite other parts.
asks: Is it safe to read and write together?
How do I update a file?

facts: Opening a file establishes a connection between the program and the data on the storage device.
The read function retrieves data from the file into the program's memory for processing.
The write function sends data from the program's memory out to the file.
Calling the close function releases the operating system's lock on the file, making it available to others.

quiz.say: Which function must be called first to access file data?
quiz.why: You must open the file to establish a connection before reading or writing.

wrong.1: Reading only works if the file is already open and connected.
wrong.2: Writing data requires an active, open connection to the file.
wrong.3: Closing the file ends the connection; it does not start one.

quiz.say: If you want to save a new score, which sequence of actions is best?
quiz.why: This sequence ensures the file is ready, the data is saved, and the connection is properly terminated.

wrong.1: Reading is not necessary if you are only adding new data.
wrong.2: You cannot write data if you close the file before writing.
wrong.3: You only need to open the file once at the beginning.

quiz.say: What is the primary purpose of the close function?

options.show: To free system resources and prevent data loss.
options.say: To free system resources and prevent data loss.

options.show: To read all the data immediately.
options.say: To read all the data immediately.

quiz.why: Closing the file ensures all buffered data is written correctly and the file lock is released.

wrong.1: Closing only disconnects; it does not delete the file itself.
wrong.2: Reading is done with the read function, not the close function.
wrong.3: Changing the file name requires a separate system command.
